request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 1:
A: record_for_host runs where("lower(host) = ?") on every embed request, replacing the previous in-memory-cached SiteSetting comparison, and the migration creates no index on the host column. Every reader of every page embedding Discourse comments now costs an extra DB roundtrip (plus an unindexed scan) on the hottest anonymous path, so high-traffic embedding sites take a per-request DB load increase at deploy time.
B: Embed hot path performance regression: `ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, issuing a DB query (`WHERE lower(host) = ?`) on every `/embed/comments` request, replacing the process-cached `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` which required zero DB traffic; the host list should be cached (process/Redis, invalidated on host CRUD) instead of queried per request

PAIR 2:
A: The per-request embed allow-list check changed from the in-memory cached SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, which runs an uncached `WHERE lower(host) = ?` query on every embed request, and the migration creates no index on host. Every embedded page's /embed/comments hit now costs a DB round trip (a scan, since a plain index would not serve lower()) — high-embed-traffic sites lose the previous zero-DB allow-list path and gain load proportional to embed views.
B: The referer check on the embed/comments hot path changed from a cached in-process SiteSetting read to an unconditional per-request SQL query — EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? runs `where("lower(host) = ?")` against a column with no index. Every render of an embedded comments iframe now adds a database roundtrip (a non-sargable full scan) where the previous check cost zero DB reads, adding load that scales with embed traffic on popular sites.
